prompts.name: 01-characters
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production concept art for Veyra, a grounded science fiction singleplayer RPG set on an inhabited planet undergoing centuries of terraforming. Style: stylised realism, real proportions with modest heroic emphasis, bold economical silhouettes, soft bevels on manufactured edges, painted material feeling, localized wear where use explains it; high quality professional game concept painting, restrained surface detail. Palette: charcoal concrete and steel, aged ivory composite, muted teal, ochre and oxide red, sparse amber utility light. Human technology is maintained and physically understandable. Strange but tangible, quiet frontier life and institutional scale. No fantasy motifs, no neon cyberpunk, no medieval armor, no franchise logos or recognizable borrowed designs, no oversaturated glow, no tiny decorative greebles. This is a proposal, not an existing game screenshot.
Primary request: A landscape character design sheet containing FIVE distinct full-body adult human characters in relaxed three-quarter standing poses, all head-to-boot visible, separated on warm pale grey background. Left to right: 01 independent surveyor, lean silhouette, long split weather coat in faded ochre over light ivory reinforced field clothes, asymmetric scanner forearm cuff and compact pack with a single tall folded probe, holding a palm-sized survey instrument; 02 Borough freight runner, broad silhouette, cropped oxide-red work jacket, sturdy trouser legs, worn cargo harness with recognizable rectangular standard cargo latches, mechanical knee brace, hair visible, holding a folded cargo manifest slate; 03 Continuity field medic, medium build, muted teal split tunic over grey flexible protective undersuit, white hard-shell medical satchel, small neck implant and hood resting down, compact sampling tool; 04 Pelagic infrastructure warden, heavier block silhouette, charcoal work armor with pale shoulder panel, enclosed practical helmet with narrow smoked visor, low-slung compact industrial carbine held safely pointed down, restrained amber status indicators; 05 independent fabricator, older stocky woman, ivory tool apron over navy coveralls, one chunky articulated prosthetic forearm, oxide-red replacement knee panel, belt with two big recognizable tools, open face. Diverse ages, skin tones and genders, ordinary working people with personal histories. Clothing must work for adventure as well as daily life. Under each character only the large two-digit number 01 02 03 04 05. No other text. Add a narrow lower strip of five dark silhouette thumbnails in the same order. Consistent scale, readable hands, legible outfits, clear negative space between figures. Avoid giant guns, excessive tactical webbing and five versions of a space soldier.

Primary request: A landscape industrial design sheet of EIGHT separate portable equipment concepts, each in clear three-quarter view, on warm pale grey paper in a roomy 4 by 2 grid, consistently lit. Number only 01 through 08. 01 compact hand survey receiver with large inset amber screen and thick fold-out antenna loop, muted ochre casing; 02 forearm implant interface cuff, age-ivory crescent housing around soft black liner, three large recessed contacts, understated teal indicator; 03 compact pulse carbine with short thick rectangular receiver, inset battery cartridge and shoulder stock, charcoal and ivory, plausible hand grips; 04 insulated induction repair tool shaped as a short U-shaped clamp with a replaceable copper head and oxide-red grip; 05 field medical cassette, small ivory clamshell with a teal fold-out handle and removable injector rack; 06 porous pale ceramic filter cartridge with black end seals and two bold connector rings, obviously a replaceable machine component; 07 standard hand-carried cargo canister with chunky beveled ivory shell, two identical black latch sockets and oxide-red lid, the connector shape also used on industrial cargo; 08 compact walk-behind scout drone, low body supported by FOUR short articulated legs, muted teal sensor head and a single folded probe. Distinct silhouettes, practical interfaces. Mild signs of repairs and salt weathering. These should be easy to identify in inventory thumbnails. One object per cell, no bullets or explanatory labels, no human hands or floating holograms, no excessive rivets or decorative machinery.

Primary request: A landscape xenobiology concept sheet with FOUR original alien animals in a roomy 2 by 2 composition, whole bodies visible in three-quarter or profile views, off-white background with small habitat swatches behind their feet. Beneath each creature use only number 01,02,03,04 and a small flat grey human silhouette to show comparative scale. All four belong to one coherent native lineage: bilateral bodies with six load-bearing limbs arranged in three pairs, smooth layered dermal shields, flexible neck, paired sensory slits instead of familiar mammal faces, subdued mineral blue-green, earth ochre, mauve and bone colors. 01 reedback: an adult wetland grazer about horse-sized, long low flexible neck and blunt scraping mouth, three pairs of sturdy legs and broad spreading toes, a small ridge of flexible gill-like dorsal sails; placid but uncanny. 02 latchmaw: a lean pursuit predator about large-dog sized, six springy folded limbs, low armored wedge head with SIDEWAYS folding jaw plates, torso longer than head, no dorsal fins, an athletic stalking pose. 03 siltbell: small amphibious scavenger about badger-sized, broad low mantle body and six stubby splayed limbs, rounded hanging throat sac and soft mud-colored shield plates, moist but not slimy, rooting beside wet stones. 04 glasswing: a long-bodied marsh glider about crane-sized, six limbs, rear four short hook feet while the front pair support wide translucent ribbed membrane wings, small blunt sensory head, shown banking just above a patch of reeds. Alien anatomy must be clear, limb pairs visible rather than vague blended legs. Beautiful unfamiliar ecology, plausible tissue and weight, species differentiated strongly in silhouette. Avoid dinosaurs, literal Earth insects, horse faces, fantasy dragons, bioluminescent decoration, skeletal horror and repeated armored quadrupeds.

Primary request: A landscape architectural design sheet arranged as FOUR generous separate three-quarter exterior vignettes on warm pale grey. Same daylight and painterly materials. Each shows one modest occupied building, a human scale figure, clearly visible entrance and loading or services side. Number only 01 through 04. 01 LANDING service module: old age-ivory molded composite shell with large rounded corners, thick oval windows, slightly domed roof, roof tank, a repaired muted-teal hatch and an added small canvas awning, simple friendly manufactured mass. 02 BOROUGH workshop-house: two irregular stacked reused modules on a short concrete plinth, oxide-red lower workshop shutter, ochre upper panels, offset covered balcony, corrugated shed extension and cistern, a walkable side stair, individual repair history. 03 PELAGIC pump and fabrication annex: squat charcoal concrete block with deep chamfered piers and slit windows, single monumental recessed pedestrian entrance beside a separate broad loading bay, dark pipe manifold and insulated upper catwalk, stern institutional scale but only two storeys. 04 CONTINUITY field station: adapted old ivory Landing module with muted teal panel insertions, a sheltered accessible porch, separate small sample room, simple three-prong sensor mast and isolated wash station, functional restrained scientific presence. Detailed enough to distinguish material families and reusable parts, simple enough for procedural building recipes. Each building fully contained in its vignette, no panorama, no invented futuristic skyline, no giant signs, no text besides numbers. Avoid modern suburban houses, cozy cottages, glass skyscrapers, faceted low-poly and cluttered greebles.

Primary request: A landscape industrial production concept design sheet on warm pale-grey background, six machines in a spacious 3 by 2 grid, numbered only 01 through 06. Clear three-quarter views, every machine entirely visible, small grey 1.7m human scale silhouettes for the first five. Technology of a modest independent frontier workshop, age-ivory cast shells, dark structural steel, teal functional panels, sparse oxide-red replacements and amber utility lights. 01 BORE EXTRACTOR, footprint about 4m square and 4m tall: three broad adjustable braced feet hold a clear central vertical reciprocating drill housing, one offset stocky flywheel and black drive belt cover, modest service platform, BIG removable sealed ore hopper on one side. 02 BRINE SKID, about 3m long: low rectangular skid with a barrel-shaped filter body, one big ivory cartridge sleeve, short clearly visible intake hose and two black hose couplings, no tower. 03 POWER AND BUFFER UNIT, about 2m high: broad short pedestal with an upright finned radiator and two dark slide-out battery drawers, amber status beacon, no solar panels. 04 WORKSHOP FABRICATOR, about 4m wide and 3m tall: squat enclosed machine with split doors, a viewing slit, a visible heavy chuck inside, material input rack on one side and finished-part tray on the other, connected coolant barrel, clear production presence. 05 ROUTE CRAWLER, about 5m long: low six-wheeled autonomous freight vehicle, rounded dark-teal front sensor housing, no driver cabin, open flat load deck bearing TWO removable standard sealed cargo pods, the pods have age-ivory beveled shells and identical large black mechanical latch sockets, oxide-red lids. 06 STANDARD FREIGHT POD detached, about 1m long, closeup of the same beveled ivory shell and same two chunky black latch sockets, stackable and sealed, a small near-side latch detail inset. Coherent reusable interface design; broad mechanisms rather than tiny pipes. No pipelines connecting the six separate cells, no arbitrary floating bits, no tiny text, no weapons, no huge megafactory or conveyor labyrinth.

Primary request: A wide landscape hero scene of a small independent extraction and fabrication yard in the Serein Basin, viewed at walking height from a service-road bend. The place must tell the resource logistics story through physical placement. Warm clear morning light on rain-darkened gravel, imported woodland and yellow-green marsh grass with an unfamiliar horse-sized six-legged native grazer near the distant reeds. In the foreground a worn compact SIX-WHEELED autonomous cargo crawler arrives on a dirt service road with two sealed ivory beveled cargo pods with oxide-red lids and chunky black latch sockets, road leads toward the yard's covered loading dock. At the yard edge a 4m-tall braced bore extractor with central drill housing and removable sealed hopper stands on three broad adjustable feet, well clear of the workshop. Beside it a waist-height brine filter skid with short intake hose toward drainage ditch. A short cable trench safely connects a finned power/battery pedestal to the equipment. The modest two-storey workshop is a reused rounded ivory composite shell, expanded with dark structural steel, corrugated shed roof and muted-teal panels; a huge fabrication machine is visible through the broad OPEN workshop door. Cargo pod storage under an awning, clean pedestrian path, a few residents: surveyor with ochre split coat and probe pack, older woman fabricator with ivory apron and prosthetic forearm, freight runner in oxide-red jacket speaking beside the dock. Down the road a small bus stop and distant charcoal Pelagic service block give regional context. Far on ridge, three huge dark atmospheric exchange towers anchor the horizon, 120-180m tall, tiny red warning lights. Large recognizable shapes, lived-in uneven investment, believable human working space and cargo access. Use simplified stylised realistic assets and richer natural terrain, consistent original Veyra aesthetic. Sparse work lights, no glowing neon, no fantasy, no franchise designs, no dense pipes everywhere, no conveyor maze, no text or logos. Buildings and machines dominate subject, landscape supports them.
